previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease, prior CABG and stents, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, diabetes, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted for chest pain that occurred during walking at his dialysis center. The pain was associated with nausea and vomiting, and did not respond to sublingual nitroglycerin. He was treated with morphine in the emergency department and admitted for evaluation of unstable angina. Initial ECG showed T-wave flattening and ST depression, but troponin levels remained stable. A cardiac catheterization revealed in-stent restenosis in the left circumflex artery and a narrowing at the origin of the LAD, both of which were treated with percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty without stent placement. He remained pain-free post-procedure, received two hemodialysis sessions during admission, and was discharged home in stable condition. Medications were adjusted, including uptitration of metoprolol and lisinopril, and he was given clear instructions on activity, diet, weight monitoring, and follow-up care.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  A ___ male with right lung crackles.  Assess for
pneumonia.

COMPARISONS:  Multiple priors including ___ and CT ___.

PA AND LATERAL CHEST:  Severe cardiomegaly is unchanged.  Similarly, evidence
of prior CABG including multiple sternal wires is stable.  A dual-lead
pacemaker projects over the right upper outer chest, new compared to the
previous examination.  Right atrial and right ventricular leads appear
appropriately positioned.  A long a segment of lateral pleural thickening
within the right lower lobe with associated blunting of the right costophrenic
angle is overall stable compared to multiple prior examinations.  Linear
opacities at the right lung base most likely represents atelectasis and also
appear stable. There are no focal new areas of consolidation.  No left pleural
effusion.  The pulmonary vascularity appears within normal limits.

IMPRESSION:  Severe cardiomegaly without evidence of congestive heart failure.
Unchanged right loculated pleural fluid and pleural thickening with associated
atelectasis.  No radiographic evidence of consolidation.

A wet reading was provided to the ED dashboard.

INDICATION:  Patient is a ___ male with right upper quadrant pain and
elevated LFTs.  Evaluate for gallstones.

EXAMINATION:  Focused abdominal ultrasound of the liver and gallbladder.

COMPARISONS:  Comparison to prior CT of the abdomen and pelvis from ___.

FINDINGS:  The liver demonstrates no focal or textural abnormalities.  The
main portal vein is patent with appropriate hepatopetal flow.  There is no
intra- or extra-hepatic biliary dilatation with the common bile duct measuring
0.45 cm in its greatest diameter.  There is cholelithiasis with gallstones
seen within the gallbladder neck without secondary signs of cholecystitis.
Specifically, no pericholecystic fluid, gallbladder wall thickening or edema,
or distention is identified.  There was a negative sonographic ___ sign.
Note is made of a nondependent 3-mm focal isoechoic lesion within the
gallbladder lumen, with characteristics most compatible with a benign
gallbladder polyp.  The spleen measures 12.6 cm and is unremarkable in
appearance.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Cholelithiasis with gallstones seen within the gallbladder neck without
secondary signs of cholecystitis.

2.  3-mm gallbladder polyp.
